channel.title: Los Angeles Review of Books – Reviews
channel.description: Book reviews from the Los Angeles Review of Books.

item.title: Murky Effects
item.description: A novel of desire and domestic disorder amid a disintegrating literary establishment.

item.title: Evidence Isn’t Always Enough
item.description: A new book explores the ‘evidence revolution,’ whose aim is to ground consequential decisions in evidence rather than opinion.

item.title: Revelatory Life
item.description: Clare Carlisle asks—what is the relationship between biography and philosophy?

item.title: Such Sights to Show You
item.description: On Shintaro Kago, manga master of the ‘erotic grotesque nonsense’ genre.

item.title: War Bros
item.description: Sharon Weinberger’s new book exposes the extent to which the US government has bound itself to the ‘arsenal of the broligarchy.’

item.title: California Sons: Miriam Pawel’s “The Browns of California”
item.description: Jake Wertz reviews “The Browns of California,” a four-generation biography of the Brown family and a portrait of the state they shaped.

item.title: Nobody, Falling Through the Darkness
item.description: Emma Cline’s new novel chronicles the final days of a man who never knew himself.

item.title: What a Long, Strange Trip
item.description: Grace Krilanovich’s new novel reads as if the Summer of Love took a time machine back to the 19th century.

item.title: She Wrote Me a Letter
item.description: Do Virginia Woolf’s uncollected letters raise the author’s stature, or lower it?

item.title: The Old Dog Stays
item.description: War through the eyes of a soldier’s best friend.

item.title: The Magic of Sisterhood
item.description: Meg Howrey discusses her new coming-of-middle-age novel about Alzheimer’s, three adult sisters, and grace in last requests.

item.title: Response to Mike Fortun Regarding ‘Original Sin’
item.description: Jonathan Basile addresses Mike Fortun’s counterpoint regarding Kathryn Paige Harden’s controversial new book.

item.title: Whither, Then, Are You Speeding, O Russia of Mine?
item.description: Two new books analyze Russia’s messianic civilizational mission under Putin.

item.title: The Empire of Information
item.description: Roopika Risam’s new book shows how various data regimes, from clay tablets in ancient Mesopotamia to today’s biometric databases, shaped human lives.
